notes.title: Acquisitions and Unaudited Pro-Forma Financial Information
text: 9 - Acquisitions and Unaudited Pro-Forma Financial Information
August 27, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of Victorville Treasure Holdings, LLC (“Victorville”), a California
limited liability company that owns and operates a 155-room hotel located at 15494 Palmdale Road, Victorville, California (the “Property”).
Under the transaction, the Company acquired 100 % of the issued and outstanding equity interests, and Victorville became a wholly owned
subsidiary of the Company upon closing.
consideration, the Company issued 216,667 shares of its Series C Convertible Preferred Stock, having an estimated fair value of $ 39,000,060 ,
based on the as-converted value of the underlying common shares using the $ 0.03 closing stock price on the acquisition date.
Victorville acquisition represents a strategic expansion of the Company’s hospitality portfolio. The Company believes the acquisition
Strengthening its presence in key hospitality markets;
Operational synergies with the Company’s existing hotel platform;
Immediate revenue contribution from ongoing hotel operations;
Enhanced scale to support an integrated lodging and guest-services strategy; and
Access to franchise-branding opportunities following planned renovations.
acquisition was accounted for in accordance with ASC 805, Business Combinations. The purchase price allocation was finalized during the
year ended June 30, 2026 within the one (1) year measurement period.
connection with the acquisition, the Agreement provides for additional contingent consideration payable to the Sellers. Under the terms
of the Agreement, the Sellers may earn up to 41,667 additional shares of Series C Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Earnout Shares”)
upon achieving specified post-closing operational and property-level milestones, including:
completion and build-out of a gym facility;
enrollment of at least fifty (50) active gym members;
completion of all remaining renovations required to meet prospective franchise brand standards; and
operation of the property under a major franchise brand for a minimum of thirty (30) days.

packaging distribution, Robotics-as-a-Service and hotel operations. The discontinuation represents a strategic shift with a major effect
on the Company’s operations and financial results, and the business is presented as discontinued operations under ASC 205-20 for
all periods presented, with prior period amounts reclassified to conform.
June 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company had no remaining assets of the discontinued operations. Liabilities of discontinued operations of

consolidated balance sheets. No exit costs, impairment losses or restructuring charges were recognized in connection with the discontinuation.

text: to June 30, 2026, the Company had the following transactions:
July 8, 2026 and September 10, 2026, the Company issued convertible notes to an accredited investor with face amounts of $ 294,118 and
$ 176,471 , respectively, for net proceeds of $ 238,000 and $ 143,000 , respectively. The face amounts include original issue discounts of
$ 44,118 and $ 26,471 , respectively, and the Company paid debt issuance costs of $ 12,000 and $ 7,000 , respectively. The notes bear interest
at 15 % per annum, payable in common stock, increasing to 24 % on an event of default, and mature July 8, 2027 and September 10, 2027 ,
respectively. The original issue discount on each note increases by 10 % of the total outstanding balance on each anniversary of the issuance
date until the note is no longer outstanding.
notes are convertible at the lower of $ 0.033 /share or 80 % of the lowest closing price during the ten ( 10 ) trading days before conversion.
The 80 % decreases to 70 % if, beginning sixty ( 60 ) days after issuance, the Company does not maintain a reserve of three (3) times the
shares issuable on full conversion, and to 50 % while the common stock is subject to a Depository Trust Company chill. The holder may
deduct $ 1,750 from the amount converted on each conversion to cover its fees, may adopt any more favorable terms the Company grants to
another investor while the notes are outstanding, and may not convert to the extent it would own more than 4.99 % of the outstanding common
stock, which it may increase to 9.99 % on sixty-one ( 61 ) days’ notice. The Company may prepay each note at 110 % of principal and
accrued interest during the first one hundred eighty ( 180 ) days and at 120 % thereafter on seven ( 7 ) days’ notice, during which
the holder may convert. On a sale of substantially all assets, merger or similar event, the holder may require redemption at 150 % of
principal plus accrued interest. Events of default include failure to maintain the share reserve, a default on any other note of the
